canonical_name: Edmonds-Karp maximum-flow correctness and polynomial-complexity theorem family (exact conjunction open)
literal_source_claim_en: A polynomial-time algorithm for maximum flow.
source_attribution: Jack Edmonds/Richard Karp; 1972 (catalog metadata and bibliographic DOI crosscheck)
statement_blocker: The Stage1-bearing catalog record says only 'a polynomial-time algorithm for maximum flow'. It does not define the network, capacity and flow domains, source/sink hypotheses, residual semantics, breadth-first augmenting-path rule, output, correctness theorem, cost model, or exact polynomial bound. A companion non-Stage1 computer-science record says O(VE^2), but importing that clause as authority would broaden this target. The 1972 paper's bibliographic identity was crosschecked, while its primary text could not be inspected. Selecting a precise proposition now would invent or substitute mathematics.
target_decision: retain the Edmonds-Karp correctness-and-complexity family at provisional H1/M4/R4, freeze no canonical proposition, and require primary-text review plus explicit reconciliation of polynomial versus O(VE^2) scope
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix a finite directed network or edge-indexed multigraph, vertex and edge universes, distinguished source and sink, a capacity codomain, flow and residual representations, executable or relational state, and the cost/input-size model.
conclusion: Open: a source-selected conjunction or separation of feasible-flow preservation, termination, maximum-flow correctness, optional minimum-cut certificate, and a precise worst-case polynomial bound such as O(V * E^2).
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: termination and maximum-flow correctness of repeated BFS-shortest residual augmentation on finite directed networks with natural capacities
the usual worst-case O(V * E^2) complexity theorem under an explicitly fixed elementary-operation and edge-count model
a checked conjunction of correctness, maximum-flow/minimum-cut certification, and the complexity bound
an executable queue-based implementation related to an abstract shortest-residual-path transition system
a generalization from integral capacities to rational or real capacities when the source and termination proof permit it
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty or singleton vertex type and source equal to sink
no source-to-sink path, no edges, or zero maximum flow
zero-capacity edges, self-loops, parallel edges, and antiparallel edges
integral versus rational or real capacities and fractional bottlenecks
zero-length paths and forward/reverse residual-edge identity
multiple BFS-shortest augmenting paths and tie breaking
whether V and E count all represented or only active edges
excluded_substitutions: arbitrary-path Ford-Fulkerson in place of breadth-first shortest augmentation
maximum-flow/minimum-cut alone without the Edmonds-Karp algorithm and complexity result
Dinic, push-relabel, capacity scaling, or bipartite matching
undirected SimpleGraph shortest-walk distance presented as a residual directed network
a fixed graph example, enumeration, timing experiment, native evaluation, or unchecked certificate
a structure or hypothesis storing a maximum flow, optimal cut, path oracle, or desired complexity bound
the companion THM-C-0097 O(VE^2) gloss silently imported as the Stage1 root
the catalog's untrusted verified label, DOI metadata, bounded no-match search, or API probe treated as proof credit
